title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless spec ships TODAY — the countdown item is now due
bullets.summary: The largest MCP revision since launch lands today: the initialize/initialized handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header are removed (version/client info/capabilities move inline into a _meta field, so any request can hit any instance behind a plain load balancer), Roots/Sampling/Logging are deprecated under a new 12-month Active->Deprecated->Removed policy, missing-resource error shifts -32002 -> -32602, six SEPs make MCP servers OAuth 2.1 resource servers, and the two first-class extensions ship — MCP Apps (sandboxed HTML UIs) and stateless Tasks (tasks/get|update|cancel, tasks/list removed).
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs is now on the breaking side of the line; the migration + least-authority hardening inventory is due today rather than deferrable, and the stateless Tasks extension maps straight onto our long-running Lens/Prism/Pulse scan jobs. Load-bearing plumbing action of the week and the clock has run out.

bullets.title: Vertical MCP-server wave compounds: Pipedrive CRM (Jul 24), Revid.ai video (Jul 16), Sprinklr (Jul 15); MCP now 10,000+ servers
bullets.summary: Pipedrive's native CRM MCP went GA Jul 24 (search deals, create/update records, schedule activities, live data with permissions + full audit trail); Revid.ai's video MCP exposes render_video->schedule_publish->publish_now; Sprinklr's Summer '26 MCP surfaces social/insight data inside Claude/Copilot/ChatGPT — against MCP crossing 10,000+ servers and 100M monthly downloads.
bullets.how: Revid's render->schedule->publish surface is a drop-in content pipeline for Brand 9 Signs signage creatives and Pulse's owned-presence video cadence; the CRM MCPs are exactly the operator wedge PRAGMA sells. Any server we adopt must be validated against today's stateless spec (item 1) before wiring it in.

bullets.title: Anthropic: Opus 5 holds as fleet default; Cowork unifies to one home across web/mobile/desktop; Claude Code + Cowork clear FedRAMP High
bullets.summary: Opus 5 (Jul 24) remains the newest Opus tier at $5/$25 per 1M (fast mode 2.5x faster at 2x cost); Chat and Cowork now share one sidebar/search/home for Projects & Artifacts with background + scheduled tasks that follow you across devices; Claude Code + Cowork are now available in a FedRAMP High authorized environment via Claude for Government.
bullets.how: No model rewire (Opus 5 stays default), but the unified Cowork home + offline scheduled-task guarantee hardens the Pulse/Lens fire schedule, and FedRAMP High opens regulated/government signage and AI-operator work as a credible PRAGMA lane.

bullets.title: arXiv: automated prompt optimization for LLM agents — descriptor + action-selection modules refined by an environment-return evolutionary loop
bullets.summary: Frames agent prompts not as static strings but as two separable, independently-optimizable modules — a goal-conditioned descriptor (what did I see) and an action selector (what do I do next) — each refined by an LLM-driven evolutionary loop guided by measured environment returns.
bullets.how: Our scan fleet's prompts are exactly this observation->action shape; splitting perception from action and scoring each against a reward signal is a concrete design input for tightening the idempotent Pulse/Lens/Prism scan logic without hand-tuning.

bullets.title: Frontier field crowded and well-funded: GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.5; Perplexity ~$200M, Cognition $1B, Glean $180M
bullets.summary: The rest of the frontier is seated: OpenAI's three-tier GPT-5.6 family (Jul 9), Google's cheap high-volume Gemini 3.6 Flash (Jul 21), xAI's 500K-context Grok 4.5 (Jul 8), Meta Muse Spark 1.1 — against a July that saw $1.8B+ raised across 12+ agent deals on hard ARR.
bullets.how: Watch, don't switch: Opus 5 remains the default, Gemini 3.6 Flash stays the cheap-batch option, and the funding wave confirms the operator-agent thesis PRAGMA is built on. No rewire.

praxis_lesson: The countdown arrived. The MCP stateless spec that has been 'N days out' all week ships today, so the migration + least-authority inventory is no longer a plan to sequence — it is a task to execute before end of day; when a deadline lands, the correct move is completion, not another round of re-prioritization. Underneath it the throughline holds: the ecosystem keeps handing us pre-built operator surfaces (CRM, video, social), so the Construct's durable edge is orchestration — but every surface we adopt now inherits today's stateless contract, so validate against the new spec before wiring anything in.
